scenario.name: Citizen Lab FORCEDENTRY, Google Project Zero & Apple CVE-2021-30860 — iOS JBIG2 Stream & MVT Shutdown/DataUsage Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a courier dropping off a fake animated greeting card that secretly conceals a dense architectural blueprint folded inside a paper disguise. Because the greeting-card label tricks the building’s automated preview booth into routing it around the armored inspection chamber, a tiny built-in typesetting machine executes seventy thousand logic steps to hijack the phone, leaving no permanent tools behind after a reboot, only crash slips and permanent cellular billing entries under a made-up maintenance worker’s name. In this scenario (T1203, Citizen Lab FORCEDENTRY, Google Project Zero & Apple CVE-2021-30860, iOS JBIG2 Stream & MVT Shutdown/DataUsage Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval, then coreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment, then dataUsage.sqlite. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval, then CoreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment, then DataUsage.sqlite, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1203 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval via IMTransferAgent & attachment-dir Audit
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1203 - Exploitation for Client Execution)
stages.description: A silent incoming delivery lands in the phone’s attachment tray stamped as a harmless animated picture, but peeling back the outer wrapper reveals a compressed document stream engineered to slip straight into the core rendering office. When a zero-click iMessage attachment (.gif wrapping a PDF/JBIG2 stream) arrives from Apple Push Notification service (APNs), IMTransferAgent automatically downloads the attachment from iCloud MMCS servers into ~/Library/SMS/Attachments/ without user interaction (logged in Linux Audit Event 101 with ProcessName=IMTransferAgent, AttachmentPath=~/Library/SMS/Attachments/9f/15/FA812B/IMG_0041.gif, HeaderMismatch=File extension .gif contains %PDF-1.3 header with /Filter /JBIG2Decode so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes mvt-ios check-backup --iocs pegasus_forcedentry.stix2 /cases/ios_backup_decrypted/ (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1203 during "Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval via IMTransferAgent & attachment-dir Audit"). Next, the follow-up artifact sqlite3 sms.db "SELECT rowid, filename, mime_type, total_bytes FROM attachment WHERE filename LIKE '%.gif';" runs (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , sqlite3 sms.db "SELECT rowid, filename, mime_type, total_bytes FROM attachment so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1203 during "Zero-Click iMessage Attachment Retrieval via IMTransferAgent & attachment-dir Audit" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/IMTransferServices.framework/IMTransferAgent / ⇠#1 ACK 101) from Node ① (#1 iMessage Attachment Delivery) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 DataUsage.sqlite & CrashReporter).

stages.title: Stage 2: CoreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment Integer Overflow (CVE-2021-30860) CrashReporter Trace
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1203 - Exploitation for Client Execution)
stages.description: When the building’s graphics press tries to lay out the disguised document outside the armored inspection chamber, the seventy-thousand-step typesetting script overflows the press’s internal counter and constructs a miniature virtual machine out of ink logic gates, leaving a crash slip in the maintenance tray. As CoreGraphics renders the masqueraded attachment outside the BlastDoor sandboxed image path, the JBIG2Stream::readTextRegionSeg parser processes over 70,000 segment commands using bitwise AND/OR/XOR/XNOR refinement operators, leaving diagnostic traces in CrashReporter and system logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 30860 with VulnerabilityId=CVE-2021-30860 , FORCEDENTRY CoreGraphics JBIG2 Integer Overflow, TargetProcess=IMTranscoderAgent / SpringBoard, ForensicArtifact=/private/var/mobile/Library/Logs/CrashReporter/IMTranscoderAgent-*.ips so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact mvt-ios check-fs --output /cases/mvt_out/ /cases/ios_filesystem_dump/ runs (which Runs Mobile Verification Toolkit , mvt-ios / mvt-android forensic parsers or inspects cellular GRX/IPX GTP-C/GTP-U roaming signaling , mvt-ios chec so that identifies zero-click mobile spyware execution traces, kernel driver privilege escalation, or anomalous cross-carrier roaming tunnels , T1203 during "CoreGraphics Xpdf JBIG2Decode Segment Integer Overflow , CVE-2021-30860 CrashReporter Trace"). stages.title: Stage 3: DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite Masqueraded Process Network Attribution
stages.subtitle: Command and Control (T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols)
stages.description: Although the spyware sweeps its temporary hallway tools away cleanly and vanishes on reboot, the phone’s permanent network billing ledgers forever keep a timestamped row showing a mystery worker with no official company badge sending megabytes of data seven seconds after the rigged card arrived. Even after the staged files under /private/var/tmp/ are deleted (since Pegasus runs purely in memory and does not persist across reboots), iOS SQLite databases DataUsage.sqlite and netusage.sqlite permanently record cellular and Wi-Fi byte counts attributed to anomalous process names (such as RoleAccountd or Stagingd) with zero bundle ID (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with DatabaseArtifact=/private/var/wireless/Library/Databases/DataUsage.sqlite , ZPROCESS / ZLIVEUSAGE, AnomalousProcessName=RoleAccountd , ZPROCNAME with NULL ZBUNDLENAME, TemporalCorrelation=Spawned 7 seconds after IMTransferAgent attachment download so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIIN, ZLIVEUSAGE.ZWIFIOUT, datetime(ZPROCESS.ZFIRSTTIMESTAMP+978307200,'unixepoch') FROM ZLIVEUSAGE JOIN ZPROCESS ON ZLIVEUSAGE.ZHASPROCESS = ZPROCESS.Z_PK WHERE ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME IS NULL;" (which executes a structured SQL query or database administration command , sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite "SELECT ZPROCESS.ZPROCNAME, ZPROCESS.ZBUNDLENAME, ZLI so that pivots from database query access or SQL injection to direct operating system command execution or authentication bypass , T1071.001 during "DataUsage.sqlite & netusage.sqlite Masqueraded Process Network Attribution" under the database daemon's service account). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ sqlite3 DataUsage.sqlite ZPROCESS ZPROCNAME=RoleAccountd ZBUNDLENAME=NULL / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 IMTransferAgent & BlastDoor) to Node ④ (#4 CoreGraphics JBIG2 Parser), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 DataUsage.sqlite & CrashReporter).
